summary: @c1-ease/card exfiltrates install host metadata to hardcoded VPS on postinstall and require
details: The package ships a postinstall hook (`node beacon.cjs`) and a `main` (`index.js`) that both invoke a `fire()` function which POSTs `os.hostname()`, the install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and the Node/npm version to a hardcoded non-publisher endpoint at `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc`. TLS certificate verification is explicitly disabled (`rejectUnauthorized: false`). The only other runtime behavior is `module.exports = new Proxy({},...)` returning a no-op for every property access, so the package has no legitimate functionality — the beacon is the entire payload. The scoped name and `Compatibility shim` self-description are consistent with a dependency-confusion placeholder targeting an internal `@c1-ease/*` namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
